label: Keep warnings out of saved notes
title: Stopped a safety warning from being replayed in the next session
summary: I fixed a bug where a one-time safety-stop message was saved as a task and shown again at the start of the next session.
cvLine: Fixed session-summary generation in an AI coding-agent hook so safety-classifier notices are no longer persisted and re-injected into later sessions; added regression tests covering the filtered, notice-only and mid-sentence cases

story.title: Stop old warnings from coming back as tasks
story.lead: ECC saves a short summary at the end of each coding session and shows it at the start of the next one. A safety-stop message was ending up in that summary.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When a response was stopped by the safety classifier, the notice was saved as if the user had asked for it. The next session then showed it again as a past task, which could trigger the same warning repeatedly.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I made the summary step ignore messages that start with that safety-stop notice, while keeping any normal message that only mentions the phrase in the middle of a sentence.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests for this; the session-end test file passes (21 of 21) and two of the new tests fail without the fix. I could not trigger a real safety stop, so the notice shape comes from the issue report.

title: Stopped the first command from timing out while a sandbox starts
summary: I fixed a bug where a command sent to a sandbox that was still starting up was treated as a one-off job and timed out, instead of running in a proper terminal.
cvLine: Fixed deferred sandbox startup in an AI security-testing agent so backends declare terminal (PTY) support up front and the first shell command keeps its interactive session; added regression tests, including one on the SDK's real local sandbox client

story.title: Make the first command work while the sandbox is still starting
story.lead: Strix can start its sandbox in the background so the agent does not have to wait. Until it finished starting, it told the tools that terminals were not available.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: While the sandbox was still starting, it reported that it had no terminal support. The agent library checked this straight away, so it left out the tool for typing into a running command and ran the first command as a one-off job. That command then hit a hard time limit and never returned a session to continue with.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: Each sandbox backend now says up front whether it supports terminals, and the built-in Docker one does. The still-starting sandbox repeats that answer until it is ready, then goes back to asking the real sandbox. Backends that do not say anything behave as before.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests, including the bug report's reproduction using the library's real local sandbox. The test file passes with 13 tests. The full suite has the same 19 failures as the main branch, and the code checks (ruff, mypy, bandit) pass.

label: Wait for provider reset before retrying
diagramTitle: Schedule heartbeat retries after limit reset
title: Stopped heartbeat retries from hammering providers after usage limit errors
summary: I fixed a bug where agent heartbeats retried every 30 seconds after hitting a provider usage limit, scheduling a single retry after the reset time instead.
cvLine: Fixed agent heartbeat retry scheduler to extract UTC usage-limit reset times and schedule a single retry at reset plus one minute, preventing provider retry storms; validated with comprehensive unit and database integration tests

story.title: Stop heartbeat retry storms after provider usage limits
story.lead: When an agent run hit a provider usage limit error, the retry scheduler hammered the provider every 30 seconds until attempts were exhausted.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Ordinary transient retries kept hammering the provider every ~30s after a usage-limit error (e.g. You've hit your limit · resets 3pm), wasting API calls while the quota window remained exhausted.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I added a helper to parse the UTC reset clock from error messages or structured retryNotBefore values, capped limit retries at 1 attempt, and scheduled the retry at reset time plus 1 minute. Ambiguous reset clocks cleanly suppress fast retries.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: Validated with 31 passing unit tests and a database integration test in Vitest, along with passing module boundary and map checks.

story.title: Report successful Prem AI calls as successful
story.lead: OpenLIT records traces of AI calls. With Prem AI, normal calls that worked were being recorded as errors and without token counts.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Recent Prem AI versions return their replies as objects rather than plain dictionaries. OpenLIT read them as dictionaries, hit an error, and so every successful non-streaming chat and embedding call was recorded as an error with no token usage.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I reused the conversion that OpenLIT already applied to streamed replies for the non-streaming chat and embedding calls, so the reply is turned into a dictionary before it is read. An embedding reply without usage data no longer causes an error either.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: In an offline before-and-after check with the real Prem AI 0.3.107 reply types, the calls went from ERROR with no token counts to OK with token counts, finish reason and response id. The new and existing Prem AI tests give 21 passing, and pylint scores 10.00/10.
